nodes.label: Single-writer resource ownership pattern
nodes.rationale: Each Python service is the sole owner of exactly one resource domain (Database owns gmail_agent.db, Accounts owns credentials/OAuth, User_data owns Gmail/Calendar clients, Vector DB owns Chroma, MCP owns LLM orchestration) so ownership boundaries stay unambiguous and only the Gateway is publicly reachable, keeping rate-limit checks and business logic out of the Gateway.

nodes.label: X7: duplicated dead data_recorder.py
nodes.rationale: data_recorder.py existed twice (under utilities/ and data_utils/), identical and imported by nothing; consolidated to one copy in backend/libs/common/ during the split, but it remains imported by nothing.

nodes.label: Hourly inactive-bucket cleanup
nodes.rationale: Inactive buckets (no access for 24 hours) are automatically removed every hour to prevent memory leaks in long-running services.

nodes.label: Fail-Open Design
nodes.rationale: If the rate limiter service is down, requests proceed rather than being blocked, because the Python client is designed to fail open so an optional dependency never becomes a hard outage.

nodes.label: Rate limiter fails open when unavailable
nodes.norm_label: rate limiter fails open when unavailable
nodes.rationale: When running Python services without the Go rate limiter, the Python rate-limiter client fails open gracefully so requests proceed without disruption rather than blocking all traffic on an optional dependency.

nodes.label: X2: GET /api/users leaks all tenants' accounts
nodes.norm_label: x2: get /api/users leaks all tenants' accounts
nodes.rationale: GET /api/users with no account_id returns every email account across all tenants; preserved verbatim to keep the golden suite green.

nodes.label: Go sync server writes straight to SQLite (documented exception)
nodes.norm_label: go sync server writes straight to sqlite (documented exception)
nodes.rationale: The Database service is the sole Python owner of gmail_agent.db, but the Go sync server on :8001 opens the same file directly to INSERT into emails and SELECT email_tokens. This is a deliberate, documented exception to single-writer ownership, kept because rewriting the Go writer was out of scope; it also makes backend/go-server/ immovable since its DBPath is a relative path.

nodes.label: 'new_emails' means fetched, not newly saved
nodes.rationale: GET /api/sync reports new_emails as the number of messages fetched, not the number newly written to the database. In the Go branch these numbers coincide; in the Python fallback branch the count diverges whenever a message_id repeats. Kept verbatim because it is pinned by two golden test files.

nodes.label: X10: blocking calls inside async def handlers
nodes.norm_label: x10: blocking calls inside async def handlers
nodes.rationale: requests.post to the Go server, googleapiclient calls, and limiter.check all block the event loop inside async handlers. The split added synchronous httpx credential fetches, the same class of problem, but this is accepted as no regression rather than fixed.

nodes.label: X3: emails.message_id has no unique constraint
nodes.norm_label: x3: emails.message_id has no unique constraint
nodes.rationale: Email lookups use filter_by(message_id=...).first(), so if two mailboxes cache the same message an arbitrary row wins; preserved as a pre-existing defect.

nodes.label: X5: thread_id is always NULL
nodes.rationale: thread_id is never populated by either sync path but is still returned by the email-details response; kept unchanged to preserve observable behavior.

nodes.label: X1: Sign-up account-takeover vector
nodes.rationale: POST /api/auth/signup with an email that already exists and any password returns a working session for somebody else's tenant. Deliberately left unfixed because fixing it changes observable behavior, which the behavior-preserving refactor was forbidden to do; tracked as its own ticket.

nodes.label: Note: reset rate limiter before running tests
nodes.norm_label: note: reset rate limiter before running tests
nodes.rationale: The e2e tests are integration tests that make actual HTTP calls and consume rate-limiter tokens, so the rate limiter must be cleared before testing to avoid assert errors from mismatched remaining-token counts.

nodes.label: X6: invalid local SLM model string with trailing whitespace
nodes.norm_label: x6: invalid local slm model string with trailing whitespace
nodes.rationale: The local SLM model string is 'qwen3.8:27b-mlx  ' - not a valid model name and has trailing whitespace. Moved into config during the split but left verbatim rather than corrected.

nodes.label: X9: last_sync_time is process-local and stale
nodes.norm_label: x9: last_sync_time is process-local and stale
nodes.rationale: The MCP last_sync_time context value is process-local, resets on restart, and is never updated by the public GET /api/sync; kept unchanged across the refactor.

nodes.label: Interactive OAuth runs inside a web request
nodes.norm_label: interactive oauth runs inside a web request
nodes.rationale: When a mailbox token cannot be refreshed, the credential ladder falls through to InstalledAppFlow.run_local_server(port=8080), an interactive browser flow started on the server inside an HTTP request. It is wrapped in run_in_threadpool and given a 120s Gateway timeout so it no longer blocks the event loop, but the fundamental shape (a hung re-auth degrades sign-in for everyone) is unchanged from before the refactor and was left as-is to preserve behavior.
